title.zh: 卷230 列傳十七 武理堪 武纳格 阿什达尔汉 鄂莫克图 吉思哈 康喀勒
title.en: Volume 230 Biographies 17: Wu Likan, Wu Nage, A Shen Da Er Han, E Moketu, Ji Siha, Kang Kalei
title.raw: 卷230 列傳十七 武理堪 武纳格 阿什达尔汉 鄂莫克图 吉思哈 康喀勒

sentences.zh: 孫達哩吉思哈弟吉普喀達吳巴海康喀勒從兄子和托瑪拉

translations.literal: Grandsons Daliji, Sihadi, Jipu, Kada, Wuba, Haikang Kalei, and the cousin's son Hetomala.
translations.idiomatic: Their grandsons Daliji, Sihadi, Jipu, Kada, Wuba, and Haikang Kalei, together with the cousin's son Hetomala.

sentences.zh: 兄孫通嘉薩璧翰}}武理堪，瓜爾佳氏，世居義屯。

translations.literal: Wu Likan, of the Guwalgiya clan, had for generations lived at Yitun.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Likan belonged to the Guwalgiya clan; his family had long resided at Yitun.

sentences.zh: 父伊蘭柱，徙居哈達費德里。

translations.literal: His father Yilanzhu moved to dwell at Hada Fedeli.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yilanzhu later relocated the family to Hada Fedeli.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起，武理堪來歸。

translations.literal: When the Taizu first rose, Wu Likan came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first raised his standard, Wu Likan came over to his side.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳，葉赫糾九部之師，三道來侵，上遣武理堪出東路偵敵。

translations.literal: In the year guisi, Yehe mustered the armies of the nine tribes and invaded by three routes; the sovereign sent Wu Likan out by the eastern route to reconnoiter the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year, Yehe rallied the forces of nine tribes and attacked along three roads. The sovereign dispatched Wu Likan by the eastern route to scout the enemy.

sentences.zh: 武理堪出虎攔哈達新城，行將百里，方度嶺，群鴉競噪，若阻其行者，武理堪心異之，度行且與敵左，馳歸告上，上命改道自札喀路向渾河部。

translations.literal: Wu Likan left from Hulan Hada New City; he had gone nearly a hundred li and was just crossing a ridge when crows clamored as if blocking his way. Wu Likan thought this strange, judged that continuing would bring him alongside the enemy, galloped back to report to the sovereign, and the sovereign ordered a change of route by the Zhaka road toward the Hun River district.
translations.idiomatic: Setting out from Hulan Hada New City, Wu Likan had marched nearly a hundred li and was crossing a pass when a flock of crows rose in a raucous clamor, as though to bar his path. Troubled by the omen, he reckoned that pressing on would put him abreast of the enemy, rode back at speed to report, and the sovereign ordered him to take the Zhaka road instead toward the Hun River country.

sentences.zh: 武理堪行，薄暮至渾河，敵方屯北岸會食，爨火密如星。

translations.literal: Wu Likan went on; at dusk he reached the Hun River. The enemy were encamped on the north bank taking their meal, and cooking fires were thick as stars.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Likan pressed on and reached the Hun River at dusk. The enemy were camped on the north bank at supper, their cook-fires scattered thick as stars.

sentences.zh: 武理堪得葉赫邏卒一，言敵兵三萬，將夜度沙濟嶺而進，遂挾以還報，時夜方半，上命旦日出師。

translations.literal: Wu Likan captured one Yehe scout, who said the enemy numbered thirty thousand and would cross Shaji Ridge by night to advance; he took him back to report. It was then midnight, and the sovereign ordered the army out at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He seized a Yehe scout who reported thirty thousand enemy troops intending to cross Shaji Ridge under cover of night. Taking the man with him, he returned to report; the night was half spent, and the sovereign ordered the host to march at daybreak.

sentences.zh: 武理堪慮我軍怵敵眾，言曰：「敵雖​​眾，心不一，誰能禦我？

translations.literal: Wu Likan feared our troops would be daunted by the enemy's numbers and said, "Though the enemy are many, their hearts are not one—who can withstand us?"
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that our men would shrink before the enemy's numbers, Wu Likan said, "They may be many, but their hearts are divided—who can stand against us?"

sentences.zh: 」及戰，遂破諸路兵。

translations.literal: " When battle was joined, the forces on every route were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fighting that followed, the armies on every route were broken.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，武理堪隸滿洲正白旗，分轄丁戶，為牛錄額真。

translations.literal: When the banners were fixed, Wu Likan was assigned to the Manchu Plain White Banner, allotted households under his jurisdiction, and made a niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: After the banner system was established, Wu Likan was placed in the Manchu Plain White Banner, given charge of households, and appointed niru captain.

sentences.zh: 出從征伐，率選鋒前驅，為噶布什賢噶喇昂邦。

translations.literal: On campaigns he went out with the army, leading the vanguard of picked troops, and served as gabsihiyan gūsa i da.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he marched with the host, leading picked vanguard troops, and held the post of commander of the brave guards.

sentences.zh: 天命四年，明經略楊鎬合諸鎮兵四道來侵，太祖督諸貝勒帥師御之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianming, Ming Grand Secretary Yang Hao united the garrison troops of the four routes to invade; the Taizu personally supervised the beile in leading the army to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianming, the Ming Grand Secretary Yang Hao combined provincial forces in four columns for an invasion, and Taizu himself oversaw the beile as they led the army to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 既，敗其三道，獨總兵李如柏出鴉鶻關，未與我師遇，鎬檄使引還。

translations.literal: Thereafter three routes were defeated; only Regional Commander Li Rubai came out through Yahuguan and had not yet met our army when Hao sent orders for him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Three of the columns were soon defeated. Only Regional Commander Li Rubai, coming out through Yahuguan, had not yet encountered our forces when Hao ordered him recalled by dispatch.

sentences.zh: 武理堪方率二十騎邏虎攔山，見如柏軍行山麓；

translations.literal: Wu Likan was then leading twenty horsemen along Hulan Mountain and saw Rubai's army marching at the foot of the hills;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Likan happened to be leading twenty horsemen along Hulan Mountain when he saw Rubai's troops moving along the foothills;

sentences.zh: 乃令諸騎立馬山巔，鳴螺，脫帽系弓末，揮且噪，若指揮伏兵者，如柏軍望而愕顧。

translations.literal: He then ordered the riders to halt their horses on the ridge crest, sound conch horns, take off their caps and tie them to the ends of their bows, wave and shout as if directing hidden troops; Rubai's army looked up in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: He had his men rein up on the ridge, blow conchs, tie their caps to their bow-tips, and wave and shout as though directing an ambush. Rubai's troops looked up in startled confusion.

sentences.zh: 武理堪遂縱騎疾馳下擊，斬四十人，獲馬五十匹，如柏軍奪路走，相蹂藉死者復千餘。

translations.literal: Wu Likan then loosed his horsemen in a swift charge down the slope, beheaded forty men, and captured fifty horses. Rubai's army broke for the road in flight, and more than a thousand died trampling one another.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Likan then spurred his riders down in a headlong charge, killing forty men and taking fifty horses. Rubai's force fled pell-mell along the road, and over a thousand more perished in the crush.

sentences.zh: 武理堪尋卒，太祖歎曰：「武理堪從朕摧鋒陷陣，幾死者數矣！

translations.literal: Wu Likan soon died. The Taizu sighed and said, "Wu Likan followed me in smashing the enemy line and charging the ranks—he was near death several times!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Likan died not long after. Taizu sighed and said, "Wu Likan followed me through the hottest fighting and was brought to death's door more than once!"

sentences.zh: 」乃錄其二子吳拜、蘇拜。

translations.literal: " He then enrolled his two sons Wubai and Subai.
translations.idiomatic: " He then took his two sons Wubai and Subai into service.

sentences.zh: 吳拜，年十六，從太祖伐明，略撫順，遇敵輒奮鬥，矢中顙不顧。

translations.literal: Wubai, at sixteen, followed the Taizu in campaigning against Ming, raiding Fushun; whenever he met the enemy he fought fiercely, and though an arrow struck his forehead he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Wubai was sixteen when he followed Taizu against the Ming in the raid on Fushun. He always flung himself into the fight, and when an arrow struck his forehead he did not so much as pause.

sentences.zh: 嘗從太祖獵，有熊突圍出，躍上峻嶺，太祖遙望見一人躍馬射熊，貫胸而墮。

translations.literal: Once on a hunt with the Taizu a bear broke from the beat and leaped up a steep ridge; from afar the Taizu saw a man spur his horse, shoot the bear, and pierce it through the chest so that it fell.
translations.idiomatic: Once while hunting with Taizu, a bear broke cover and scrambled up a steep ridge. From a distance Taizu saw a rider spur after it, shoot the beast through the chest, and bring it tumbling down.

sentences.zh: 上顧侍臣雅蓀曰：「是非吳拜不能。

translations.literal: The sovereign turned to attendant Yasun and said, "No one but Wubai could have done that."
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign turned to his attendant Yasun and said, "Only Wubai could have done that."

sentences.zh: 」遣視之，吳拜也。

translations.literal: " He sent someone to look—it was Wubai.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent men to see: it was Wubai.

sentences.zh: 因諭諸皇子曰：「吳拜之勇，今共見之矣！

translations.literal: He then addressed the princes: "You have all seen Wubai's valor today!"
translations.idiomatic: He then told the princes, "You have all witnessed Wubai's courage today!"

sentences.zh: 」遂授侍衛。

translations.literal: " He then appointed him an imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made him an imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 天命四年，從伐葉赫，負重創，力戰不退，師還，賜良馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianming he followed the campaign against Yehe, suffered grave wounds, fought on without yielding, and when the army returned was given a fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianming he joined the attack on Yehe, took severe wounds, and fought on without giving ground. When the army returned, he was rewarded with a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 明總兵毛文龍誘我新附之眾實皮島。

translations.literal: Ming Regional Commander Mao Wenlong enticed our newly submitted people to Pidao.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming regional commander Mao Wenlong lured away our newly submitted people to Pidao.

sentences.zh: 吳拜循徼三日，獲逋八十餘，射殺文龍使者，還告上。

translations.literal: Wubai patrolled the frontier for three days, captured more than eighty fugitives, shot dead one of Wenlong's envoys, and returned to report to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Wubai patrolled the border for three days, seized more than eighty deserters, killed one of Wenlong's messengers, and returned to report.

sentences.zh: 時吳拜已代父為牛錄額真，上命以所獲隸所轄牛錄。

translations.literal: By then Wubai had succeeded his father as niru ejen; the sovereign ordered that those captured be assigned to the niru under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Wubai had by then succeeded his father as niru captain, and the sovereign ordered that the captives be enrolled in the niru under his command.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐明。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed a campaign against Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined a campaign against the Ming.

sentences.zh: 破明軍於南壽山，授備禦。

translations.literal: He defeated Ming forces at Nanshou Mountain and was appointed a beiyu.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Ming troops at Nanshou Mountain and was appointed deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 既克遼陽，以俘獲分隸諸將，上以吳拜能繼父志，年少建功，命視一等大臣，隸千人。

translations.literal: After Liaoyang was taken, captives were distributed among the generals; because Wubai could carry on his father's will and had won merit while young, the sovereign ordered that he be treated as a first-rank minister and given command of a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: After the capture of Liaoyang, booty and captives were parceled out among the commanders. Seeing that Wubai had upheld his father's legacy and won distinction while still young, the sovereign treated him as a minister of the first rank and placed a thousand men under him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，蒙古巴林部貝勒囊努兔背盟掠境上，上遣將討之，吳拜從，諜者為敵困，援之出，殪敵百人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Mongol Balin beile Nangnuhu broke the alliance and raided the border; the sovereign sent generals to punish him, and Wubai followed. Scouts were trapped by the enemy; he rescued them and killed a hundred of the foe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Balin Mongol beile Nangnuhu broke faith and raided the frontier. Wubai joined the punitive expedition sent against him, rescued scouts whom the enemy had surrounded, and killed a hundred of the raiders.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，列十六大臣，佐鑲白旗。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Wubai was ranked among the sixteen great ministers and assisted the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, Wubai was named one of the sixteen great ministers and served with the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 命逐蒙古亡去者，至都爾弼。

translations.literal: He was ordered to pursue Mongol deserters as far as Duerbi.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to pursue Mongol fugitives as far as Duerbi.

sentences.zh: 蒙古亡去者十五人，拒戰，吳拜既被創，仍奮擊，盡斬之。

translations.literal: Fifteen Mongol deserters resisted; though Wubai was wounded, he fought on fiercely and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen fugitive Mongols stood and fought. Though Wubai was wounded, he pressed the attack and cut them down to the last man.

sentences.zh: 太宗諭諸大臣曰：「是固先帝數嘉許者！

translations.literal: Taizong told the ministers, "This is indeed one whom the late emperor praised again and again!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told the ministers, "This is the man my late brother praised time and again!"

sentences.zh: 」賞特厚。

translations.literal: " He rewarded him with exceptional generosity.
translations.idiomatic: " He rewarded him with exceptional largesse.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，伐明，取永平、灤州等四城，吳拜從貝勒阿敏守永平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong, on a campaign against Ming, Yongping, Luanzhou, and four other cities were taken; Wubai followed Beile Amin in garrisoning Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiancong, during a campaign against the Ming, Yongping, Luanzhou, and four other cities were captured. Wubai followed Beile Amin in holding Yongping.

sentences.zh: 阿敏引還，吳拜當坐罪逮系，以嘗率擺牙喇兵援灤州，夜入敵營，太宗命貰之，釋其縛。

translations.literal: When Amin withdrew, Wubai was liable to punishment and arrested; because he had once led the bayalara troops to relieve Luanzhou and entered the enemy camp by night, Taizong ordered him pardoned and his bonds loosed.
translations.idiomatic: When Amin pulled back, Wubai was held culpable and placed in bonds. But because he had once led the bayalara to relieve Luanzhou and raided the enemy camp by night, Taizong pardoned him and had him released.

sentences.zh: 尋授噶布什賢甲喇章京。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed gabsihiyan jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed colonel of the brave guards.

sentences.zh: 五年，從伐明，圍大凌河城，與甲喇章京蘇達喇詣錦州偵敵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed a campaign against Ming and besieged Dalinhe city; with Jalan Janggin Sudara he went to Jinzhou to spy on the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined the Ming campaign and took part in the siege of Dalinhe, then went with Colonel Sudara to Jinzhou to reconnoiter the enemy.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐察哈爾，率精騎前驅，道遇蒙古亡去者，擊殺之，察哈爾林丹汗西奔土默特部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the campaign against Chahar, leading picked cavalry in the van; on the road he met Mongol deserters and killed them. Chahar's Ligdan Khan fled west to the Tumed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he marched against Chahar at the head of elite cavalry, cut down Mongol fugitives encountered on the march, and pursued Ligdan Khan of Chahar as he fled west into Tumed territory.

sentences.zh: 師還，取歸化城，上命吳拜撫輯降者。

translations.literal: When the army returned it took Guihua city; the sovereign ordered Wubai to pacify and settle those who submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march Guihua was taken, and the sovereign charged Wubai with pacifying the surrendered population.

sentences.zh: 八年，伐明，攻大同，多爾濟將中軍，圖魯什將左軍，吳拜將右軍，明總兵曹文詔迎戰，擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, campaigning against Ming, they attacked Datong: Dorji commanded the center, Tursi the left, and Wubai the right. Ming Regional Commander Cao Wenchao met them in battle and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on a Ming campaign against Datong, Dorji led the center, Tursi the left, and Wubai the right. The Ming regional commander Cao Wenchao gave battle and was routed.

sentences.zh: 復與甲喇章京席特庫設伏宣府，獲明守備一，殲其遊騎。

translations.literal: Again with Jalan Janggin Xituku he laid an ambush at Xuanfu, captured one Ming garrison commander, and destroyed their patrol cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Colonel Xituku in an ambush at Xuanfu, took a Ming garrison commander, and wiped out the enemy patrol horse.

sentences.zh: 尋與承政阿什達爾漢等招林丹汗子額哲來歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, with Cheng Zheng Ashi Daerhan and others, he induced Ligdan Khan's son Eje to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Grand Secretary Ashi Daerhan and others in winning over Ligdan Khan's son Eje, who came in submission.

sentences.zh: 九年五月，明屯軍大凌河西，吳拜與固山額真阿山、石廷柱、圖賴要其歸路，斬明副將劉應選，獲游擊曹得功及守備三，殲步騎五百餘，复攻克松山城南堡。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year Ming troops were encamped west of the Dalin River; Wubai, with Gūsa Ejen Ashan, Shi Tingzhu, and Tulai, blocked their line of retreat, beheaded Ming Vice Commander Liu Yingxuan, captured Brigadier Cao Degong and three garrison commanders, destroyed more than five hundred infantry and cavalry, and again stormed the southern fort of Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the ninth year, when Ming forces lay west of the Dalin River, Wubai joined Banner Commanders Ashan, Shi Tingzhu, and Tulai in cutting off their retreat. They killed the Ming vice commander Liu Yingxuan, took Brigadier Cao Degong and three garrison commanders, destroyed more than five hundred foot and horse, and seized the southern bastion of Songshan.

sentences.zh: 師還，進三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was promoted to third-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was promoted to third-rank colonel.

sentences.zh: 是時，上遣諸貝勒分道伐明，命吳拜等帥師駐上都城舊址，偵軍事。

translations.literal: At that time the sovereign sent the beile on separate routes against Ming and ordered Wubai and others to lead troops stationed at the old site of Shangdu to watch military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the sovereign sent the beile on several routes against the Ming and ordered Wubai and others to hold the old site of Shangdu with a force to watch enemy movements.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，復命與勞薩等齎書投明邊吏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he was again ordered, with Laosa and others, to carry letters and deliver them to Ming border officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde he was again ordered, with Laosa and others, to carry dispatches to Ming frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 冬，徵朝鮮，命與承政馬福塔等率兵三百為前驅，襲朝鮮都城，朝鮮王倧走南漢山城。

translations.literal: In winter, on the expedition against Korea, he was ordered with Cheng Zheng Mafuta and others to lead three hundred men as vanguard, strike the Korean capital, and King Wang Jeon fled to Namhansanseong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the Korean expedition, he and Grand Secretary Mafuta were ordered to lead three hundred men as vanguard, storm the Korean capital, and drive King Jeon to Namhansanseong.

sentences.zh: 師進，吳拜與勞薩擊破朝鮮援兵，斬二百餘級。

translations.literal: As the army advanced, Wubai and Laosa defeated Korean reinforcements and beheaded more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: As the army advanced, Wubai and Laosa routed Korean reinforcements and took more than two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 二年，授噶布什賢噶喇昂邦，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed gabsihiyan gūsa i da and ranked among the deliberative ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made commander of the brave guards and named among the deliberative ministers.

sentences.zh: 甲喇章京丹岱、阿爾津等如土默特互市，將還，命吳拜率將校至歸化城迎護，遇明邏卒十六人，斬其十五，獲馬十九，俘一，以還。

translations.literal: Jalan Janggin Dantai, A'erjin, and others went to Tumed for trade and were about to return; Wubai was ordered to lead officers to Guihua to meet and escort them. They met sixteen Ming border soldiers, killed fifteen, captured nineteen horses and one prisoner, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Colonels Dantai and A'erjin went to Tumed for trade and were returning, Wubai was sent with officers to Guihua to meet them. They fell in with sixteen Ming border troops, killed fifteen, seized nineteen horses and one captive, and came back.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，略寧遠，逐敵墮壕，斬馘甚眾。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he raided Ningyuan, drove the enemy into ditches, and killed and beheaded many.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he raided Ningyuan, chased the enemy into the trenches, and killed a great number.

sentences.zh: 八月，率兵八十人至洪山口，遇明兵，斬其裨將；

translations.literal: In the eighth month he led eighty men to Hongshankou, met Ming troops, and beheaded their adjutant;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he led eighty men to Hongshankou, encountered Ming forces, and killed their adjutant;

sentences.zh: 复擊走羅文峪騎兵五百，奪其纛，獲馬四十，殲密雲步兵百餘。

translations.literal: again routed five hundred cavalry at Luowenyu, seized their standard, captured forty horses, and destroyed more than a hundred infantry at Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: then routed five hundred cavalry at Luowenyu, took their banner, captured forty horses, and wiped out more than a hundred infantry at Miyun.

sentences.zh: 五年，與勞薩率兵過中後所，略海濱，斬級二百，獲馬騾牲畜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, with Laosa, he led troops past Zhonghousuo, raided the seacoast, took two hundred heads, and captured horses, mules, and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he and Laosa led troops past Zhonghousuo, raided the coast, took two hundred heads, and seized horses, mules, and livestock.

sentences.zh: 我師攻錦州，命吳拜駐軍要隘為策應，屢敗敵兵。

translations.literal: When our army attacked Jinzhou, Wubai was ordered to garrison a strategic pass as support and repeatedly defeated enemy troops.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Jinzhou, Wubai was posted at a key pass in support and repeatedly routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 六年春，以攻錦州勿克，論統師王貝勒罪，吳拜坐罰鍰。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, because the attack on Jinzhou had not succeeded, the commanding prince beile was judged at fault; Wubai was fined.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year, when the assault on Jinzhou failed, the prince in overall command was held culpable and Wubai was fined.

sentences.zh: 秋，上自將攻松山，明兵敗走，吳拜未邀擊，逮系，旋命釋之。

translations.literal: In autumn the sovereign personally led the attack on Songshan; Ming troops were defeated and fled, but Wubai had not intercepted them. He was arrested, then soon ordered released.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the sovereign led the attack on Songshan in person. Ming forces broke and fled, but Wubai had failed to cut them off. He was placed in bonds and soon afterward released.

sentences.zh: 七年，從貝勒阿巴泰入明邊，敗敵豐潤、三河、靜海，至於青州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Beile Abatai into Ming territory, defeated the enemy at Fengrun, Sanhe, and Jinghai, and reached Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed Beile Abatai into Ming territory, defeated the enemy at Fengrun, Sanhe, and Jinghai, and pushed as far as Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗取明中後所、前屯衛。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang in taking Ming Zhonghousuo and Qiantunwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang in capturing Ming Zhonghousuo and Qiantunwei.

sentences.zh: 十一月，复授正白旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was again appointed meire ejen of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was again appointed vice-banner commander of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關，擊李自成。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the entry through the passes and attacked Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shunzhi reign he marched through the passes and fought Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 二年，解梅勒額真，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year he was relieved of the post of meire ejen and appointed an inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he gave up the vice-banner command and was appointed an inner minister.

sentences.zh: 三年，從豫親王多鐸討蘇尼特部長騰機思。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Yu Dodo in punishing Tengjisi, chief of the Sunite.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Prince Yu Dodo against Tengjisi, chief of the Sunite tribe.

sentences.zh: 四年，與輔國公鞏阿岱、內大臣何洛會帥師戍宣府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, with Prince of the State Assisting the Nation Gongadai and Inner Minister Heluohei, he led troops to garrison Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined Prince Gongadai and Inner Minister Heluohei in leading a garrison force at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 論功，遇恩詔，累進二等伯。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed, on an amnesty edict he was repeatedly promoted to second-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: For his services, and under successive amnesty promotions, he rose to second-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 蘇拜，年十五，從太祖伐蒙古有功，授侍衛，兼領牛錄額真。

translations.literal: Subai, at fifteen, followed the Taizu in campaigning against the Mongols with merit, was appointed a bodyguard, and also held the post of niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Subai was fifteen when he joined Taizu's Mongol campaigns with distinction, was made an imperial guardsman, and also served as niru captain.

sentences.zh: 天聰間，從軍收察哈爾林丹汗子額哲，遂入明邊，攻代州，明兵三百自崞縣赴援，蘇拜爭先當敵，明兵潰走。

translations.literal: During Tiancong he followed the army in receiving Ligdan Khan's son Eje of Chahar, then entered Ming territory and attacked Daizhou; three hundred Ming troops came from Guoxian to relieve the city, and Subai took the lead to meet the enemy, whereupon the Ming troops broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiancong he marched in the submission of Ligdan Khan's son Eje of Chahar, then crossed into Ming territory and attacked Daizhou. When three hundred Ming troops marched from Guoxian to relieve the city, Subai took the van and drove them off in rout.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從伐朝鮮，破敵桃山村。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed the expedition against Korea and defeated the enemy at Taoshan village.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde he joined the Korean expedition and routed the enemy at Taoshan village.

sentences.zh: 三年，授擺牙喇甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed bayalara jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed colonel of the bayalara.

sentences.zh: 從貝勒岳託伐明，自牆子嶺入，越明都，擊敗明太監馮永盛。

translations.literal: He followed Beile Yuetuo against Ming, entered by Qiangziling, passed beyond the Ming capital, and defeated the Ming eunuch Feng Yongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Beile Yuetuo on a Ming campaign, entered through Qiangziling, swept past the Ming capital, and defeated the eunuch commander Feng Yongsheng.

sentences.zh: 四年，圍錦州，蘇拜屢擊敗明援兵自松山、杏山至者；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, during the siege of Jinzhou, Subai repeatedly defeated Ming reinforcements coming from Songshan and Xingshan;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, while Jinzhou was under siege, Subai repeatedly routed Ming relief columns from Songshan and Xingshan;

sentences.zh: 又與固山額真圖爾格等伏兵烏忻河口，多所俘獲，敵千餘躡​​師後，擊卻之，獲其輜重。

translations.literal: Again with Gūsa Ejen Turgene and others he ambushed at Wuxinhekou and took many captives; more than a thousand of the enemy followed the army's rear, and he beat them back and seized their baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: With Banner Commander Turgene and others he also laid an ambush at Wuxinhekou and took many prisoners. When more than a thousand enemy followed the army's rear, he drove them off and captured their baggage train.

sentences.zh: 六年，复圍錦州，敗松山騎兵，又敗明總督洪承疇所將步兵，予世職牛錄章京，兼半個前程。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again besieged Jinzhou, defeated the cavalry of Songshan, and again defeated the infantry led by Ming Governor-General Hong Chengchou; he was given the hereditary post of niru janggin with half a regular stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he again invested Jinzhou, routed the Songshan cavalry, and then broke the infantry of Governor-General Hong Chengchou. He was granted the hereditary rank of niru colonel with half a regular stipend.

sentences.zh: 七年，從貝勒阿巴泰伐明，敗敵，克樂安、昌邑。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Beile Abatai against Ming, defeated the enemy, and took Le'an and Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed Beile Abatai into Ming territory, defeated the enemy, and captured Le'an and Changyi.

sentences.zh: 八年，師還，進三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the army returned, he was promoted to third-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on the army's return, he was promoted to third-rank colonel.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關，擊李自成。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the entry through the passes and attacked Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shunzhi reign he marched through the passes and fought Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 世祖既定鼎，命將分道討自成：以豫親王多鐸為定國大將軍，出山西、河南；

translations.literal: After the Shizu had fixed the capital, he ordered generals to pursue Zicheng on separate routes: Prince Yu Dodo was made Pacifier of the State Grand General and went out through Shanxi and Henan;
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizu had established the capital, he sent armies against Zicheng on separate routes: Prince Yu Dodo was named Pacifier of the State Grand General and marched through Shanxi and Henan;

sentences.zh: 英親王阿濟格為靖遠大將軍，道塞外土默特、鄂爾多斯諸部入邊，南取西安，蘇拜佐阿濟格軍。

translations.literal: Prince Ying Ajige was made Pacifier of the Distant Grand General, entered the frontier by way of Tumed and Ordos beyond the passes, and marched south to take Xi'an; Subai assisted Ajige's army.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying Ajige was named Pacifier of the Distant Grand General, entered through Tumed and Ordos beyond the frontier, and marched south on Xi'an. Subai served on Ajige's staff.

sentences.zh: 方冬，渡黃河，鑿冰以濟。

translations.literal: It was deep winter; they crossed the Yellow River by cutting through the ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the depths of winter they crossed the Yellow River, breaking the ice to ford it.

sentences.zh: 明年春，至榆林。

translations.literal: The next spring they reached Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring they reached Yulin.

sentences.zh: 自成兵夜襲蒙古軍，蘇拜與擺牙喇纛章京徹爾布赴援，賊敗走，還軍遇伏，复擊卻之。

translations.literal: Zicheng's troops raided the Mongol army by night; Subai and Bayalara Da Janggin Cherbu went to their relief, the rebels were defeated and fled, and on the return march they met an ambush and again drove it back.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng's men attacked the Mongol force by night. Subai and Banner Colonel Cherbu went to the rescue, routed the rebels, and on the march back beat off an ambush as well.

sentences.zh: 攻延安，七戰皆勝。

translations.literal: They attacked Yan'an and won seven battles in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan'an they fought seven engagements and won them all.

sentences.zh: 自成走湖廣，追之至安陸，屢破賊壘，俘馘無算。

translations.literal: Zicheng fled to Huguang; they pursued him to Anlu, repeatedly stormed rebel stockades, and took captives and heads beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng fled into Huguang; they pursued him to Anlu, repeatedly stormed his camps, and took prisoners and heads beyond number.

sentences.zh: 三年，攝擺牙喇纛章京。

translations.literal: In the third year he acted as bayalara da janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served as acting banner colonel of the bayalara.

sentences.zh: 從肅親王豪格討張獻忠，敗獻忠將高汝礪於三寨山，進擊獻忠於西充。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Su Haoge in campaigning against Zhang Xianzhong, defeated Xianzhong's general Gao Ruli at Sanzhai Mountain, and advanced to attack Xianzhong at Xichong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Su Haoge against Zhang Xianzhong, routed Xianzhong's general Gao Ruli at Sanzhai Mountain, and pressed the attack on Xianzhong at Xichong.

sentences.zh: 賊攻正藍旗營，蘇拜與阿爾津共援之，大破賊兵。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked the Plain Blue Banner camp; Subai and A'erjin jointly went to its relief and inflicted a great defeat on the rebel troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels struck the Plain Blue Banner camp, Subai and A'erjin reinforced it together and routed the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 五年，師還，授擺牙喇纛章京。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the army returned, he was appointed bayalara da janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on the army's return, he was appointed banner colonel of the bayalara.

sentences.zh: 論功，遇恩詔，累進二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed, on amnesty edicts he was repeatedly promoted to second-rank jingqini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: For his services, and under successive amnesty promotions, he rose to second-rank jingqini hafan.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，吳拜、蘇拜及內大臣洛什、博爾輝發英親王阿濟格罪狀，吳拜進三等侯，蘇拜進一等精奇尼哈番加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year Wubai, Subai, and Inner Ministers Luoshi and Bo'erhui reported the crimes of Prince Ying Ajige; Wubai was promoted to third-rank marquis and Subai to first-rank jingqini hafan with the additional title tosara hafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year Wubai, Subai, and Inner Ministers Luoshi and Bo'erhui denounced Prince Ying Ajige. Wubai was raised to third-rank marquis and Subai to first-rank jingqini hafan with the added title tosara hafan.

sentences.zh: 二月，洛什、博爾輝以諂媚諸王、造言構釁，論死；

translations.literal: In the second month Luoshi and Bo'erhui were sentenced to death for flattering the princes and fabricating words to stir strife;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Luoshi and Bo'erhui were condemned to death for currying favor with the princes and fabricating charges to sow discord;

sentences.zh: 吳拜兄弟坐削爵，奪官，籍沒。

translations.literal: the Wubai brothers were punished by reduction of rank, loss of office, and confiscation of property.
translations.idiomatic: the Wubai brothers were stripped of rank and office and their property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 蘇拜又坐阿徇睿親王多爾兗，論死，上特宥之。

translations.literal: Subai was also judged for currying favor with Prince Rui Dorgon and sentenced to death, but the sovereign specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Subai was also condemned to death for siding with Prince Rui Dorgon, but the sovereign granted him a special pardon.

sentences.zh: 九年，起蘇拜為正白旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Subai was restored and appointed meire ejen of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Subai was restored to office as vice-banner commander of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢內大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to inner minister.

sentences.zh: 十五年，上念吳拜兄弟事太祖、太宗有戰功，复授吳拜世職一等精奇尼哈番，蘇拜一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, remembering that the Wubai brothers had served the Taizu and Taizong with military merit, the sovereign again granted Wubai the hereditary first-rank jingqini hafan and Subai the first-rank ashan i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, recalling the brothers' battlefield service under Taizu and Taizong, the sovereign restored Wubai to the hereditary rank of first-rank jingqini hafan and Subai to first-rank ashan i hafan.

sentences.zh: 尋授蘇拜領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Subai was appointed leading inner minister of the imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made chief inner minister of the imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年十二月，蘇拜卒，諡勤僖。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Kangxi, Subai died; his posthumous title was Qinxie.
translations.idiomatic: Subai died in the twelfth month of Kangxi 3 and was given the posthumous name Qinxie.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，吳拜卒，年七十，諡果壯。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year Wubai died, aged seventy; his posthumous title was Guozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wubai died in the fourth month of the following year at seventy, with the posthumous name Guozhuang.

sentences.zh: 吳拜子郎談，自有傳。

translations.literal: Wubai's son Langtan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wubai's son Langtan is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 蘇拜第三子和託，康熙間以侍衛從討王輔臣，戰平涼城北，殺賊甚眾；

translations.literal: Subai's third son Hetuo, during the Kangxi reign as a bodyguard followed the campaign against Wang Fuchen; fighting north of Pingliang city he killed very many rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Hetuo, Subai's third son, served as a bodyguard in the Kangxi era and joined the campaign against Wang Fuchen; at a battle north of Pingliang he slew many rebels;

sentences.zh: 從討吳三桂，戰攸縣，敗三桂將王國佐等；

translations.literal: following the campaign against Wu Sangui, he fought at You County and defeated Sangui's generals Wang Guozuo and others;
translations.idiomatic: He later fought Wu Sangui at You County and routed Sangui's generals Wang Guozuo and others;

sentences.zh: 戰永興，敗三桂將胡國柱等。

translations.literal: fighting at Yongxing he defeated Sangui's generals Hu Guozhu and others.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongxing he defeated Sangui's commanders Hu Guozhu and others.

sentences.zh: 十九年，自廣西進兵攻石門坎、黃草壩，薄雲南省城，敗吳世璠將胡國柄、劉起龍等，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, advancing from Guangxi he attacked Shimenkan and Huangcaoba, pressed close to Yunnan provincial city, and defeated Wu Shifan's generals Hu Guobing and Liu Qilong and others—at every point he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he advanced from Guangxi against Shimenkan and Huangcaoba, closed on the Yunnan capital, and defeated Shifan's generals Hu Guobing and Liu Qilong, earning merit throughout.

sentences.zh: 官至護軍參領，予世職騎都尉加一云騎尉。

translations.literal: He reached the office of gushan dolon, and was granted the hereditary rank of jiduwei with one additional yunjiwei.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to colonel of the guards and received the hereditary rank of jiduwei plus one yunjiwei.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-second year.

sentences.zh: 武納格，博爾濟吉特氏，隸蒙古正白旗。

translations.literal: Wu Nage, of the Borjigit clan, was enrolled in the Mongol Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Nage belonged to the Borjigit clan and was registered in the Mongol Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 其先蓋出自蒙古，而居於葉赫。

translations.literal: His ancestors had probably come forth from Mongolia but dwelt at Yehe.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were originally of Mongol stock but had settled at Yehe.

sentences.zh: 太祖創業，武納格以七十二人來歸。

translations.literal: When the Taizu founded the enterprise, Wu Nage came to submit with seventy-two men.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu was founding the state, Wu Nage submitted with seventy-two followers.

sentences.zh: 有勇略，通蒙、漢文，賜號「巴克什」。

translations.literal: He had courage and stratagem, was versed in Mongol and Chinese script, and was granted the style "Bakshi."
translations.idiomatic: Brave and resourceful, he knew both Mongol and Chinese and was honored with the title Bakshi.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，從伐烏喇有功，授三等副將。

translations.literal: In the guichou year he followed the attack on Wula with merit and was appointed third-rank vice general.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year he distinguished himself in the campaign against Wula and was made third-rank vice general.

sentences.zh: 天命十一年，太祖伐明，圍寧遠城未下，命武納格別將兵攻覺華島。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianming the Taizu attacked Ming, besieged Ningyuan city without taking it, and ordered Wu Nage separately to lead troops against Juehua Island.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 11 Taizu struck Ming and laid siege to Ningyuan without success; he then ordered Wu Nage to take a separate force against Juehua Island.

sentences.zh: 明參將姚撫民將兵四萬，倚島列屯，鑿冰為壕，袤十五里，衛以盾。

translations.literal: Ming vice general Yao Fumin commanded forty thousand troops, leaned on the island to array camps, cut ice for moats fifteen li in length, and guarded them with shields.
translations.idiomatic: Ming vice general Yao Fumin had forty thousand men entrenched along the island, with ice-cut trenches fifteen li long shielded along their length.

sentences.zh: 武納格督軍爭壕，首排盾迳入，盡殲其眾，焚所儲芻糗及舟二千餘，進三等總兵官。

translations.literal: Wu Nage supervised the army in contesting the moat; he was first to thrust through the shield line straight in, annihilated their entire force, burned stored fodder and grain and more than two thousand boats, and was advanced to third-rank zongbing guan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Nage led the assault on the trenches, broke through the shield wall at the head of the column, annihilated the garrison, burned their stores and more than two thousand boats, and was promoted to third-rank zongbing guan.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，武納格總管蒙古軍，位亞揚古利、李永芳，在八大臣上。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Wu Nage had overall charge of the Mongol army, ranked below Yangguli and Li Yongfang, above the eight great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Wu Nage commanded the Mongol forces, ranking below Yangguli and Li Yongfang but above the eight great ministers.

sentences.zh: 旋以蒙古軍益眾，分左、右二營，武納格與鄂本兌同為固山額真。

translations.literal: Soon, as the Mongol army grew larger, it was divided into left and right camps; Wu Nage and Ebendui were both appointed gushan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: As the Mongol army grew, it was split into left and right wings, with Wu Nage and Ebendui each appointed gushan ejen.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年春，與額駙蘇納等率蒙古軍，益以滿洲驍卒八十人，伐察哈爾，降其邊境二千戶。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year of Tiancong, with efuhu Suna and others he led the Mongol army, augmented by eighty stalwart Manchu soldiers, against Chahar and received the submission of two thousand households on its border.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Tiancong 3, with Imperial Son-in-law Suna and others he led the Mongol army, reinforced by eighty elite Manchu troops, against Chahar and took the surrender of two thousand border households.

sentences.zh: 軍中流言降者瞷我師寡將為變，於是盡殲其男子，惟二台吉得免，俘其孥八千。

translations.literal: In the army rumor spread that the surrendered would spy on our few soldiers and make trouble; therefore all their adult males were killed, only two taiji escaped, and eight thousand of their women and children were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors in camp held that the surrendered meant to spy on the small force and rebel; all adult males were therefore killed, only two taiji were spared, and eight thousand women and children were taken captive.

sentences.zh: 太宗責武納格等殺降非義，奪所給牲畜，命以所俘分隸二翼，贍之毋失所。

translations.literal: Taizong reproached Wu Nage and others for killing the surrendered contrary to righteousness, confiscated livestock that had been given, and ordered the captives apportioned to the two wings and supported so none lacked a home.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rebuked Wu Nage and the others for slaughtering those who had surrendered, seized the livestock that had been granted them, and ordered the captives distributed between the two wings and provided for so that none were left destitute.

sentences.zh: 冬，從太宗伐明，入龍井關，克遵化，進薄明都。

translations.literal: In winter he followed Taizong against Ming, entered Longjing Pass, took Zunhua, and advanced pressing close to the Ming capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he followed Taizong against Ming, entered Longjing Pass, took Zunhua, and pressed toward the Ming capital.

sentences.zh: 明督師袁崇煥自寧遠來援，左翼蒙古兵迎戰不能勝，武納格麾右翼蒙古兵繼進，遂敗敵。

translations.literal: Ming supreme commander Yuan Chonghuan came from Ningyuan to relieve; the left-wing Mongol troops met battle and could not prevail; Wu Nage directed the right-wing Mongol troops to advance in succession and then defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming supreme commander Yuan Chonghuan marched from Ningyuan to relieve the capital, the left-wing Mongols could not hold; Wu Nage sent the right wing forward in support and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賜俘獲之半以犒其軍。

translations.literal: He was granted half the captives to reward his army.
translations.idiomatic: Half the spoils were granted to reward his troops.

sentences.zh: 尋克固安。

translations.literal: Soon after he took Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took Gu'an as well.

sentences.zh: 四年春，克永平。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year he took Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he captured Yongping.

sentences.zh: 明將以三千騎自玉田至，武納格遣兵擊之走，獲馬百餘。

translations.literal: A Ming general came from Yutian with three thousand horse; Wu Nage sent troops to strike them and put them to flight, capturing more than a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When a Ming commander advanced from Yutian with three thousand cavalry, Wu Nage sent troops to drive him off and seized more than a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 行略豐潤，還，聞明兵四千攻大安口城急，與察哈喇赴援，解其圍。

translations.literal: On the march he raided Fengrun; on return, hearing four thousand Ming troops were urgently attacking Da'ankou city, he and Chahala went to relieve and raised the siege.
translations.idiomatic: While raiding Fengrun on the return march, he learned that four thousand Ming troops were pressing Da'ankou; he and Chahala hurried to its relief and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 又就軍士行樵，設伏致敵，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: Again, while soldiers were out gathering firewood, he set an ambush to lure the enemy and killed and captured beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while his men were out gathering firewood, he laid an ambush, drew the enemy in, and killed and captured without number.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，復從伐明。

translations.literal: In autumn of the fifth year he again followed the attack on Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year he again campaigned against Ming.

sentences.zh: 明總兵祖大壽守大凌河城，杏山守將與大壽書，謀攜軍棄城相就，武納格獲以獻，得其情，於是環城築壘鑿壕，為久困計。

translations.literal: Ming zongbing Zu Dashou held Dalinghe city; the Xingshan garrison commander exchanged letters with Dashou plotting to carry off the army, abandon the city, and join together; Wu Nage seized them and presented them, learning the truth; therefore they ringed the city building ramparts and digging moats for a long-term siege plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming commander Zu Dashou held Dalinghe, and the Xingshan garrison commander wrote to him plotting to abandon their posts and unite their forces; Wu Nage intercepted the letters and reported the plot, after which the besiegers ringed the city with ramparts and trenches for a prolonged siege.

sentences.zh: 武納格統蒙古兵屯城東南，大壽縱兵出攻我所下台堡，武納格與貝勒阿濟格等率兵夾攻，殲敵過半，自是城兵不復出。

translations.literal: Wu Nage commanded Mongol troops stationed southeast of the city; Dashou sent troops out to attack our lower fort; Wu Nage with Prince Ajige and others led troops in pincer attack and annihilated over half the enemy; from then on the city troops did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Nage held the southeast with Mongol troops; when Dashou sallied against a lower fort, Wu Nage and Prince Ajige struck from both sides and destroyed more than half his force, after which the garrison never ventured out again.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，與阿濟格招撫大同、宣府邊外察哈爾部眾。

translations.literal: In summer of the sixth year with Ajige he pacified and won over the Chahar tribes outside the borders of Datong and Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year he and Ajige won over the Chahar peoples beyond the Datong and Xuanfu borders.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，與貝勒阿巴泰等侵明，攻山海關，有所俘獲。

translations.literal: In autumn of the seventh year with Prince Abatai and others he invaded Ming, attacked Shanhaiguan, and had some captures.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year he joined Prince Abatai in an incursion against Ming, struck at Shanhaiguan, and took booty.

sentences.zh: 師還，明兵追襲，武納格為殿，力戰卻之。

translations.literal: The army returned; Ming troops pursued and attacked; Wu Nage served as rearguard and by fierce fighting repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal Ming forces pursued; Wu Nage commanded the rearguard and fought them off.

sentences.zh: 太宗諭諸貝勒大臣曰：「武納格所在建功，今又為殿敗敵。

translations.literal: Taizong instructed the princes and great ministers: "Wherever Wu Nage is he establishes merit; now again as rearguard he defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told the princes and ministers: "Wu Nage wins merit wherever he is sent; now, as rearguard, he has again beaten the enemy.

sentences.zh: 人臣為國，當如是也！

translations.literal: A minister serving the state ought to be like this!
translations.idiomatic: A subject should serve the state in just this way!

sentences.zh: 八年五月，改蒙古軍左、右營為左、右翼，以武納格為左翼固山額真。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year the Mongol army's left and right camps were changed to left and right wings, and Wu Nage was made left-wing gushan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year the Mongol left and right camps became left and right wings, and Wu Nage was named left-wing gushan ejen.

sentences.zh: 定諸將功次，武納格以一等昂邦章京世襲，旋進三等公。

translations.literal: When the merits of the generals were ranked, Wu Nage inherited as first-rank angbang janggin, and soon was advanced to third-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were ranked he received the hereditary rank of first-rank angbang janggin and was soon raised to third-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 是年，太宗复率諸貝勒分道伐明，命武納格統蒙古軍為策應，​​入獨石口，越興安嶺，經保安州，至應州，與大軍會，道收察哈爾千餘戶，所過諸州縣，或攻或撫，悉稱上意。

translations.literal: That year Taizong again led the princes in separate routes against Ming and ordered Wu Nage to command the Mongol army as support: entering Dushikou, crossing the Xing'an range, passing through Bao'an prefecture to Yingzhou, joining the main army; along the way receiving over a thousand Chahar households; the prefectures and counties passed through were attacked or pacified, all according to the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: That year Taizong again divided his forces against Ming and sent Wu Nage with the Mongols in support through Dushikou and over the Xing'an Mountains by way of Bao'an to Yingzhou, where he joined the main army; he gathered more than a thousand Chahar households en route and attacked or pacified the districts he passed as the sovereign wished.

sentences.zh: 閏八月，自得勝堡班師，收蒙古逃人自陽和入者四百七十人。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month, withdrawing from Desheng Fort, he received four hundred seventy Mongol fugitives entering from Yanghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month, marching back from Desheng Fort, he took in four hundred seventy Mongol deserters who had entered from Yanghe.

sentences.zh: 九月，喀爾喀部眾為察哈爾所襲殺，命將百人往诇，斬二十餘人而還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Khorchin tribesmen were attacked and killed by Chahar; he was ordered to take a hundred men to reconnoiter, beheaded more than twenty, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, when Khorchin tribesmen were raided by Chahar, he was sent with a hundred men to scout, killed more than twenty of the enemy, and returned.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 子德穆圖、齊墨克圖、廣泰。

translations.literal: His sons were Demutu, Qimoketu, and Guangtai.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Demutu, Qimoketu, and Guangtai.

sentences.zh: 德穆圖，武納格長子也。

translations.literal: Demutu was Wu Nage's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Demutu was Wu Nage's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 初任牛錄額真。

translations.literal: At first he served as niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He began as niru captain.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年正月，擢戶部承政。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Chongde he was promoted to bureau director of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongde 3 he was promoted to bureau director of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 七月，更定官制，改右參政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the official system was revised and he was changed to right vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, when offices were reorganized, he became right vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，從上伐明，圍松山，樹雲梯攻城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the sovereign against Ming, besieged Songshan, and erected cloud ladders to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed the sovereign against Ming, besieged Songshan, and raised siege ladders against the walls.

sentences.zh: 會明兵自錦州赴援，德穆圖度不能克，棄雲梯引還，罪當死，上特貰之，論罰。

translations.literal: When Ming troops came from Jinzhou to relieve, Demutu judged they could not be taken, abandoned the cloud ladders and withdrew; the crime merited death but the sovereign specially pardoned him and imposed a lesser penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming relief marched from Jinzhou, Demutu saw the city could not be taken, abandoned the ladders, and withdrew; though the offense was capital, the sovereign spared his life and imposed a fine instead.

sentences.zh: 尋兼任梅勒額真。

translations.literal: Soon after he was additionally appointed meire ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made meire ejen as well.

sentences.zh: 六年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗伐明，圍錦州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang against Ming and besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang against Ming and laid siege to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 蒙古貝勒諾木齊等守外城，約降，鄭親王令德穆圖迎之。

translations.literal: Mongol princes Nomuci and others held the outer city and agreed to surrender; Prince Zheng ordered Demutu to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol prince Nomuci and others held the outer city and offered to surrender; Prince Zheng ordered Demutu to receive them.

sentences.zh: 諾木齊方率所部與明兵戰，德穆圖以其子阿桑喜出我師克外城，諾木齊始來歸。

translations.literal: Nomuci was just then leading his division fighting Ming troops; Demutu sent his son Asangxi out and our army took the outer city; only then did Nomuci come to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Nomuci was still fighting Ming troops with his followers when Demutu sent out his son Asangxi; once our forces took the outer city, Nomuci at last came over.

sentences.zh: 德穆圖詭言諾木齊父子皆所拔出，論罰，籍家產之半，罷參政、梅勒額真，俾專領牛錄。

translations.literal: Demutu falsely claimed that Nomuci father and son were both drawn out by him; he was penalized, half his family property was registered and confiscated, he was removed as vice commissioner and meire ejen, and made to hold only a niru.
translations.idiomatic: Demutu falsely claimed credit for winning over Nomuci and his son; he was fined, half his estate was confiscated, stripped of his posts as vice commissioner and meire ejen, and left in charge of a niru alone.

sentences.zh: 七年，從貝勒阿巴泰伐明，自薊州入邊，薄明都，略山東。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Prince Abatai against Ming, entered the frontier from Jizhou, pressed close to the Ming capital, and raided Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed Prince Abatai against Ming, crossed in from Jizhou, pressed on the capital, and raided Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關擊流賊，授拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed entry into the passes to strike the roving bandits and was granted baitalabule hafan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he followed the army through the passes against the roving rebels and was granted baitalabule hafan.

sentences.zh: 二年，從豫親王多鐸攻潼關，遂定江南。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Prince Yu Dodo to attack Tong Pass and then pacified Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he followed Prince Yu Dodo against Tong Pass and helped pacify Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 敗明將鄭鴻逵於瓜洲，與都統馬喇希徇常州，與明將黃蜚等遇，再戰皆捷。

translations.literal: He defeated Ming general Zheng Hongkui at Guazhou; with dutong Malaxi he swept Changzhou; meeting Ming generals Huang Fei and others he fought twice and both times prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Ming general Zheng Hongkui at Guazhou, joined dutong Malaxi in taking Changzhou, and twice defeated Ming commanders led by Huang Fei.

sentences.zh: 分兵下宜興、崑山諸縣，加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: He detached troops to take Yixing, Kunshan, and other counties, and was given the added title tosara hafan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to reduce Yixing, Kunshan, and other counties and received the added title tosara hafan.

sentences.zh: 復任本旗蒙古副都統，三進一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Mongol vice dutong of his banner, and thrice advanced to first-rank adaha hafan.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Mongol vice dutong of his banner and was three times promoted to first-rank adaha hafan.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 齊墨克圖，武納格次子。

translations.literal: Qimoketu was Wu Nage's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Qimoketu was Wu Nage's second son.

sentences.zh: 早歲屢從行陣，略寧遠，敗明兵。

translations.literal: In early years he repeatedly followed the campaigning ranks, raided Ningyuan, and defeated Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he often took the field, raided Ningyuan, and defeated Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 武納格既卒，以廣泰襲世職，從伐明，坐違令不前，奪世職，以齊墨克圖降襲一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: After Wu Nage had died Guangtai inherited the hereditary office; following the attack on Ming he was punished for violating orders and not advancing, lost the hereditary office, and Qimoketu was demoted to inherit first-rank ashan i hafan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Nage's death Guangtai inherited the family rank; on campaign against Ming he was punished for disobeying orders and holding back, lost the hereditary title, and Qimoketu inherited a reduced first-rank ashan i hafan.

sentences.zh: 復從伐明，與沙爾虎達等率邏卒至錦州，明兵五百來追，還擊敗之，獲馬六十及其纛。

translations.literal: Again following the attack on Ming, with Sharhuda and others he led border troops to Jinzhou; five hundred Ming troops came in pursuit; turning back he defeated them and captured sixty horses and their standard.
translations.idiomatic: On a later Ming campaign he and Sharhuda led border troops to Jinzhou; when five hundred Ming soldiers pursued, he turned, routed them, and seized sixty horses and their banner.

sentences.zh: 太宗伐明，三圍錦州，齊墨克圖皆在軍中，遇城兵出戰，驟馬截擊，陣斬十人。

translations.literal: When Taizong attacked Ming and thrice besieged Jinzhou, Qimoketu was always in the army; when city troops came out to fight he suddenly galloped to intercept and killed ten men in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizong's three sieges of Jinzhou Qimoketu was always in the field; when the garrison sallied he charged to cut them off and killed ten men in the line.

sentences.zh: 攻洪承疇所將步卒，掩殺甚眾，又敗敵援兵。

translations.literal: Attacking the foot soldiers led by Hong Chengchou he ambushed and killed very many, and again defeated enemy relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Assaulting the infantry under Hong Chengchou he cut down great numbers in ambush and again beat back enemy reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 崇德八年三月，與阿爾津、哈寧阿等伐黑龍江，圍都里屯，克之；

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year of Chongde, with A'erjin, Haning'a, and others he campaigned on the Heilongjiang, besieged Dulitun, and took it;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Chongde 8 he joined A'erjin and Haning'a on the Heilongjiang campaign, besieged Dulitun, and captured it;

sentences.zh: 又降大小噶爾達蘇、能吉爾三屯師：賚貂皮、銀幣。

translations.literal: again brought to submission the three settlements of Greater and Lesser Ga'erdasu and Nengji'er; rewards of sable pelts and silver coin were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: he also reduced the three settlements of Greater and Lesser Ga'erdasu and Nengji'er, and was rewarded with sable pelts and silver.

sentences.zh: 十一月，擢梅勒額真，佐本旗。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was promoted to meire ejen to assist his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was promoted to meire ejen to assist his banner.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關，加拜他喇布勒哈番，合為三等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed entry into the passes, was given baitalabule hafan, combined as third-rank jingqini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he followed the entry into China, received baitalabule hafan, and held the combined rank of third-rank jingqini hafan.

sentences.zh: 三年，從定西大將軍何洛會擊破叛將賀珍。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the Pacifier of the West Grand General He Lohui and crushed the rebel general He Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served under Grand General He Lohui, Pacifier of the West, and defeated the rebel He Zhen.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，復以廣泰襲一等阿思哈尼哈番，別以齊墨克圖子薩哈炳分襲拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; again Guangtai inherited first-rank ashan i hafan, while separately Qimoketu's son Sahabing was allotted to inherit baitalabule hafan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year; Guangtai again inherited first-rank ashan i hafan, while Qimoketu's son Sahabing separately inherited baitalabule hafan.

sentences.zh: 廣泰遇恩詔，進二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: Guangtai, on amnesty edicts, was advanced to second-rank jingqini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Under successive amnesty edicts Guangtai was raised to second-rank jingqini hafan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封三等子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong the enfeoffment was fixed as third-rank zi (viscount).
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign the title was fixed as third-rank viscount.

sentences.zh: 阿什達爾漢，納喇氏，與葉赫貝勒金台石同族，為兄弟，太宗諸舅也。

translations.literal: Ashi Daerhan, of the Nara clan, was of the same clan as Yehe prince Gintaisi, brothers, and maternal uncles to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Ashi Daerhan of the Nara clan was kin to Yehe prince Gintaisi—they were brothers and maternal uncles to Taizong.

sentences.zh: 太祖滅葉赫，阿什達爾漢率所屬來歸，授牛錄額真，隸滿洲正白旗。

translations.literal: When the Taizu destroyed Yehe, Ashi Daerhan led his followers to submit, was appointed niru ejen, and was enrolled in the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu destroyed Yehe, Ashi Daerhan submitted with his followers, was made niru captain, and was registered in the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 天命六年二月，從伐明，攻奉集堡，圍其城，阿什達爾漢先諸將奮進，三月，攻遼陽，复先登，克之，授一等參將，敕免死一次。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Tianming he followed the attack on Ming, assaulted Fengji Fort and besieged its city; Ashi Daerhan advanced before the other generals; in the third month attacking Liaoyang he again was first to ascend and took it; he was appointed first-rank participant general and granted one exemption from death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianming 6 he campaigned against Ming, stormed Fengji Fort, and was first among the generals to press the assault; in the third month he was again first over the wall at Liaoyang and took the city, for which he was made first-rank participant general with one death penalty remitted.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，以阿什達爾漢典朝鮮、蒙古諸屬部，嘗奉使宣諭。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Ashi Daerhan was put in charge of Korea, Mongolia, and other subject departments, and sometimes was sent on missions to proclaim and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Ashi Daerhan oversaw Korea, Mongolia, and other subject peoples and was often sent to proclaim imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 天聰六年，明邊吏遣使議和，上命阿什達爾漢及白格、龍什等報聘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tiancong Ming border officials sent envoys to discuss peace; the sovereign ordered Ashi Daerhan, Baige, Longshi, and others to return the embassy.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 6 Ming border officials sent envoys to discuss peace; the sovereign sent Ashi Daerhan, Baige, Longshi, and others to reply.

sentences.zh: 既盟而歸，白格言阿什達爾漢及龍什等受明邊吏餽，命奪入官。

translations.literal: After the alliance they returned; Baige reported that Ashi Daerhan and Longshi and others had received gifts from Ming border officials; the order was to confiscate them for the state.
translations.idiomatic: On their return after the treaty, Baige reported that Ashi Daerhan, Longshi, and the others had accepted gifts from Ming border officials; the sovereign ordered the gifts seized for the treasury.

sentences.zh: 六年，從貝勒濟爾哈朗、薩哈璘如蒙古鞫獄，賚敕二十道，失其九，論罰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Princes Jirhalang and Sahalian to Mongolia to judge cases, was entrusted with twenty edicts, lost nine of them, and was penalized.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he accompanied Princes Jirhalang and Sahalian to Mongolia to hear cases, was entrusted with twenty edicts, lost nine, and was fined.

sentences.zh: 十一月，復以定律令頒布​​蒙古諸部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was again sent to proclaim laws and statutes to the Mongol tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was again sent to promulgate the laws among the Mongol tribes.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，上自將伐察哈爾林丹汗，命徵兵科爾沁部，會於宣府左衛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year the sovereign personally led the attack on Chahar Khan Lindan; he ordered levying troops from the Khorchin tribe to assemble at Xuanfu Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year the sovereign led the campaign against Chahar Khan Lindan in person and ordered the Khorchin to muster at Xuanfu Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 林丹汗西遁，道死。

translations.literal: Lindan Khan fled west and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Lindan Khan fled westward and died on the way.

sentences.zh: 所屬額爾德尼囊蘇等以其眾降。

translations.literal: His subordinates Erdeni Nangsu and others led their masses to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His followers Erdeni Nangsu and others brought their people in submission.

sentences.zh: 上命阿什達爾漢及吳拜等挾額爾德尼囊蘇诇林丹汗子額哲所在。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Ashi Daerhan and Wubai and others to take Erdeni Nangsu along to scout where Lindan Khan's son Eje was.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign sent Ashi Daerhan and Wubai, taking Erdeni Nangsu with them, to find Lindan Khan's son Eje.

sentences.zh: 九月，率來降台吉塞冷等還，並報復有祁他特等率千人而來者，踵相接也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he led the submitted taiji Seren and others back, and also reported in reply that Qitete and others were leading a thousand men to come, one after another in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned with the surrendered taiji Seren and others and reported that Qitete was bringing a thousand men, with more parties following close behind.

sentences.zh: 旋命至舂科爾大會蒙古諸部，分畫牧地，使各有封守，復與諸貝勒亭平其獄訟。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to go to Chungoer to assemble the Mongol tribes, divide and mark pasture lands so each had its allotted guard, and again with the princes fairly settle their lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to Chungoer to assemble the Mongols, apportion grazing lands, and, with the princes, settle their disputes.

sentences.zh: 十一月，還報稱旨，令專轄一牛錄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he returned and reported that it accorded with the intent; he was ordered to have sole jurisdiction over one niru.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he returned with a favorable report and was given sole charge of one niru.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，從貝勒多爾袞等將萬人取額哲。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year he followed Prince Dorgon and others with ten thousand men to take Eje.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year he followed Prince Dorgon with ten thousand men to take Eje.

sentences.zh: 四月，師至托里圖，多爾袞等遵上所授方略，遣阿什達爾漢及金台石孫南褚諭額哲母。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the army reached Tuolitu; Dorgon and others following the strategy the sovereign had imparted sent Ashi Daerhan and Gintaisi's grandson Nanchu to instruct Eje's mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the army reached Tuolitu; following the sovereign's plan, Dorgon sent Ashi Daerhan and Gintaisi's grandson Nanchu to reason with Eje's mother.

sentences.zh: 額哲母，金台石女孫也，阿什達爾漢為其族尊行，額哲遂從其母舉部來降。

translations.literal: Eje's mother was Gintaisi's granddaughter; Ashi Daerhan stood in the honored senior line of her clan; Eje then followed his mother and brought the whole tribe to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Eje's mother was Gintaisi's granddaughter and Ashi Daerhan her senior kinsman; persuaded through her, Eje brought his whole following in submission.

sentences.zh: 當我軍未至，有鄂爾多斯濟農圖巴者招額哲，與盟而去。

translations.literal: When our army had not yet arrived, there was Ordos jinong Tubai who had summoned Eje and, after making an alliance, departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before our army arrived, Ordos jinong Tubai had summoned Eje, made an alliance with him, and gone off.

sentences.zh: 阿什達爾漢偵知之，追及圖巴，令悉歸額哲之餽。

translations.literal: Ashi Daerhan learned this by espionage, overtook Tubai, and ordered that all be returned of what had been gifted to Eje.
translations.idiomatic: Ashi Daerhan learned of this, overtook Tubai, and compelled him to restore everything that had been given to Eje.

sentences.zh: 又率兵入明邊，略宣府、大同，入山西境，多所俘獲。

translations.literal: Again he led troops into the Ming frontier, raided Xuanfu and Datong, entered Shanxi territory, and captured a great deal.
translations.idiomatic: He again led troops into Ming territory, raided Xuanfu and Datong, crossed into Shanxi, and took abundant spoils.

sentences.zh: 師還，上親迎勞之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the sovereign went in person to welcome and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, the sovereign went out in person to welcome the troops and commend them.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年六月，授都察院承政。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Chongde he was appointed cheng zheng of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Chongde 1 he was made cheng zheng of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 上御崇政殿，侍臣巴圖魯詹、額爾克戴青後至，阿什達爾漢責其慢，叱出之。

translations.literal: The sovereign attended Chongzheng Hall; attendant ministers Batulu Jan and Erke Daiqing arrived late; Ashi Daerhan rebuked them for tardiness and drove them out.
translations.idiomatic: At Chongzheng Hall the attendant ministers Batulu Jan and Erke Daiqing arrived late. Ashi Daerhan reproached their delay and had them expelled.

sentences.zh: 十月，與希福使察哈爾、喀爾喀、科爾沁諸部，申明律令。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, with Shifu he was sent to Chahar, Khalkha, Khorchin, and other tribes to proclaim the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he and Shifu were dispatched to Chahar, Khalkha, Khorchin, and the other tribes to set forth the laws.

sentences.zh: 十二月，從伐朝鮮，國王李倧走保南漢山城，豫親王多鐸帥師追之，圍城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he followed the campaign against Korea; King Li Jong fled to hold Nanhanshan city; Prince Yu Dodo led the army in pursuit and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he joined the Korean campaign. King Li Jong withdrew into Nanhanshan city; Prince Yu Dodo led the pursuit and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮諸道援兵合萬八千人，樹二柵城外，悉眾出戰，阿什達爾漢及貝子碩託率精騎銳進，大破其軍。

translations.literal: Korean relief troops from all circuits totaled eighteen thousand; they erected two palisades outside the city and came out to fight in full force; Ashi Daerhan and Prince Shuotuo led elite cavalry forward sharply and routed their army.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces from the Korean circuits mustered eighteen thousand men, threw up two stockades outside the walls, and marched out in full strength. Ashi Daerhan and Prince Shuotuo led picked cavalry in a fierce charge and smashed them.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮別將以五千人屯山麓為聲援，復分兵百，循河而南，阿什達爾漢馳擊盡殲之，攻破其壘，餘眾皆潰。

translations.literal: A Korean deputy general with five thousand men camped on the foothills as a supporting force; again he divided a hundred troops to go south along the river; Ashi Daerhan galloped to attack and annihilated them all, stormed their stockade, and the remainder all fled.
translations.idiomatic: A Korean deputy stationed five thousand men on the hillside as a reserve and sent a hundred men south along the river. Ashi Daerhan rode down on them, wiped them out, stormed their camp, and the survivors scattered.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，倧請降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Jong petitioned to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Jong sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 論功，進三等副將，世襲。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed, he was advanced to third-rank deputy general with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he was advanced to third-rank deputy general, the rank made hereditary.

sentences.zh: 尋復使科爾沁、巴林、扎魯特、喀喇沁、土默特、阿祿諸部，頒赦，且讞獄。

translations.literal: Soon he was again sent to Khorchin, Baarin, Jarud, Kharachin, Tumed, Aru, and other tribes to proclaim an amnesty and also to judge cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent again to Khorchin, Baarin, Jarud, Kharachin, Tumed, Aru, and the other tribes to proclaim an amnesty and sit in judgment.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，部議阿什達爾漢讞獄失平，受蒙古諸部餽，命罷承政，奪所餽入官。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year the ministry deliberated that Ashi Daerhan had judged cases unfairly and accepted gifts from the Mongol tribes; he was ordered removed as cheng zheng and the gifts seized for the state.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the fifth month, the ministry found that Ashi Daerhan had judged unevenly and accepted gifts from the Mongol tribes. He was dismissed as cheng zheng and the gifts were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 七月，复授都察院承政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was again appointed cheng zheng of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was restored as cheng zheng of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 五年，與參政祖可法等疏論時事，略言：「皇上欲恢張治道，深思篤行之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, with Grand Secretary Zukefa and others he memorialized on current affairs, saying in summary: "The Emperor wishes to expand the way of governance and to reflect deeply and practice it steadfastly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined Grand Secretary Zukefa and others in a memorial on current affairs, which in summary said: "The Emperor wishes to broaden the way of rule and to think deeply and carry it out with steadfast purpose.

sentences.zh: 今諸國景附，朝廷清明，而諸王以下至諸固山額真，彼此瞻顧，第念身家，莫肯一心為國，有所論列。

translations.literal: Now all states draw near in homage and the court is clear, yet from the princes down to the gushan ejen each looks to the others and thinks only of self and family, none willing with one heart to serve the state and offer proposals.
translations.idiomatic: All the realms now draw near and the court is clear, yet from the princes down to the gushan ejen each watches the others and cares only for self and household, none willing to serve the state with one heart and set forth proposals.

sentences.zh: 不知果無可言耶，抑有所畏忌而不敢言耶？

translations.literal: Is it truly that there is nothing to say, or is it that there are fears and scruples and they dare not speak?
translations.idiomatic: Is it that there is truly nothing to say, or that they fear something and dare not speak?

sentences.zh: 夫刑所以防民之姦，骫於法則麗於刑，此不可宥也。

translations.literal: Punishment exists to guard against the people's wickedness; those who bend the law are caught by punishment—this cannot be excused.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment exists to restrain the people's wrongdoing; whoever bends the law falls under punishment, and this cannot be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 今刑部斷獄不依本律，諸臣有坐者，或從重論，輒削其職。

translations.literal: Today the Ministry of Punishment decides cases without following the fundamental statutes; when officials are found guilty, they are sometimes judged with added severity and their offices are forthwith stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Ministry of Punishment tries cases without following the basic statutes; when officials are found guilty they are sometimes sentenced more heavily than the law allows and their offices are at once stripped away.

sentences.zh: 臣思諸臣歷戰陣，出死力，蒙恩授官；

translations.literal: Your ministers reflect that these officials have passed through battle arrays and given their utmost strength, receiving grace and appointment to office;
translations.idiomatic: We reflect that these officials have fought through many battles and risked their lives, receiving grace and appointment to office;

sentences.zh: 一旦有過，豈可不論重輕而遽削其職乎？

translations.literal: once they have faults, how can their offices be suddenly stripped without weighing heavy and light?
translations.idiomatic: yet once they err, how can their offices be stripped at once without weighing the gravity of the offense?

sentences.zh: 臣等竊思先時簡選議事十人，今皆不稱職，宜罷斥。

translations.literal: Your ministers privately consider that the ten previously selected to deliberate on affairs are now all unfit for office and ought to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: We privately consider that the ten men earlier chosen to deliberate on affairs are now all unfit and ought to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 令甲，戰死者將吏得世職，兵則卹其妻孥。

translations.literal: By regulation, officers and commanders who die in battle receive hereditary posts, while soldiers' wives and children receive relief.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation, officers and commanders who die in battle receive hereditary posts, while the wives and children of common soldiers receive relief.

sentences.zh: 今又未盡行，惟皇上裁察。

translations.literal: This is again not fully carried out—may the Emperor examine and decide."
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is again not fully carried out. May the Emperor examine and decide."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the sovereign praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the sovereign commended and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐明，上督諸軍圍松山。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the campaign against Ming; the sovereign supervised the armies besieging Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the Ming campaign while the sovereign directed the armies besieging Songshan.

sentences.zh: 明總兵曹變蛟屯乳峰山，乘夜棄寨，率步騎直犯御營，諸將力戰卻之。

translations.literal: Ming zongbing Cao Bianjiao was stationed at Rufeng Mountain; seizing the night he abandoned his camp and led infantry and cavalry straight against the imperial camp; the generals fought hard and repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming zongbing Cao Bianjiao lay at Rufeng Mountain. In the night he abandoned his camp and led foot and horse straight at the imperial encampment; the generals fought fiercely and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 阿什達爾漢未至，論罪，罷承政，降世職為牛錄章京。

translations.literal: Ashi Daerhan had not arrived; judged at fault, he was removed as cheng zheng and his hereditary rank reduced to niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Ashi Daerhan had not arrived in time. He was held culpable, dismissed as cheng zheng, and his hereditary rank was reduced to niru janggin.
